title: command palette performance monitor missing 2 icon after last update

judgment.rationale: The reporter's new reply identifies the missing icons as GPU and Network, narrowing the investigation from arbitrary Performance Monitor bands to two defined glyphs. Current source maps both metrics to specific Fluent glyph codepoints, while the related merged grid FontIcon fix may cover a shared presentation boundary but is not confirmed as a fix for this issue.
evidence: The reporter supplied a screenshot from PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable on Windows 11 25H2 showing two missing Performance Monitor icons.
A PowerToys member requested the missing icon identities on 2026-09-08, and the reporter answered GPU and Network.
PerformanceMonitorCommandsProvider maps Network and NetworkSpeed to Icons.NetworkIcon and Gpu to Icons.GpuIcon.
Icons.NetworkIcon is U+EC05 and Icons.GpuIcon is U+E950.
Merged PR #50231 fixed auto-sized FontIcon clipping or loss in Command Palette grid and gallery views, but it closes #50225 and is not linked to this report.
No linked fix, assignee, or maintainer-confirmed duplicate covers #50158.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the bounded GPU/Network glyph and grid-presentation investigation design, while requesting a current reproduction only if the two entries are still missing after the #50231 release.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix is applicable if the identified glyphs are absent from the active icon font or are clipped by CmdPal presentation. The exact mechanism has not yet been reproduced on a build containing the related merged grid fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Make Performance Monitor GPU and Network glyph presentation resilient
proposed_fixes.root_cause: GPU and Network have now been identified as the missing Performance Monitor icons. Their icon definitions use U+E950 and U+EC05, respectively. The defect may be specific to those glyphs in the active icon font or may be clipping/loss in the shared CmdPal grid FontIcon container addressed for another report by PR #50231; public evidence does not yet distinguish the two.
plan: Reproduce GPU and Network Performance Monitor items on a build containing the merged grid-icon fixes and inspect their resolved FontIcon glyph, font family, size, and container bounds.
Compare the two glyph codepoints against the active Fluent icon font and a known-rendering glyph in the same template.

If the glyphs resolve but are clipped, extend the shared grid/glyph sizing fix with regression coverage; if either glyph is unavailable, replace it with a compatible Fluent glyph and cover the metric-to-icon mapping.
verification: Open Performance Monitor in the Command Palette list, grid, and gallery presentations and verify GPU and Network glyphs are visible at normal and scaled DPI.
Verify NetworkSpeed continues to use the intended Network icon and other CPU, memory, disk, and battery glyphs do not regress.
Confirm the corrected behavior after container virtualization and repeated page opening.

confidence.rationale: The affected metrics and their exact codepoints are now confirmed, but the report predates the related grid FontIcon fix and lacks a current post-fix reproduction or diagnostic evidence that distinguishes unavailable glyphs from clipping.

issue_context.summary: Two Command Palette Performance Monitor icons disappeared after the 0.101.2362 update. The new reporter response identifies them as GPU and Network, linking the visual regression to two concrete icon definitions but not yet proving whether the glyphs or their shared grid presentation is at fault.
known_information: The issue is open, marked Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, Needs-Team-Response, and Product-Command Palette, and appears in the project as Needs Attention.
The report is for PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable on Windows 11 25H2.
The reporter supplied a screenshot and a diagnostic archive, though automated triage could not analyze that archive.
A member asked which icons were missing; the reporter confirmed GPU and Network.
The current Performance Monitor provider maps GPU to U+E950 and Network to U+EC05.
PR #50231 later shipped a CmdPal grid and gallery FontIcon clipping/loss correction for a different issue.
inferences: The two missing entries may share a glyph-font compatibility characteristic rather than a metric-data failure because Performance Monitor still loads.
The merged shared presentation fix may already resolve the report in a newer build, but that is not established by the live discussion.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter supplied the missing decision-changing fact requested by the maintainer, so a generic request for icon names is no longer valid. The exact GPU and Network mappings enable a focused visual and glyph-resolution investigation. Because the screenshot came from a release preceding the related shared FontIcon correction, a short current-build confirmation is needed to avoid implementing a duplicate or choosing a replacement glyph without proving the active rendering path.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue, all four comments, labels, assignees, and project context.
Confirmed the latest reporter reply names GPU and Network as the missing icons.
Reviewed PerformanceMonitorCommandsProvider and confirmed mappings for Network, NetworkSpeed, and GPU.
Reviewed Icons.cs and confirmed NetworkIcon is U+EC05 and GpuIcon is U+E950.
Reviewed related merged PR #50231, which fixes grid and gallery FontIcon sizing/container recycling for #50225 but is not linked to this issue.
Searched live PowerToys pull requests and issue links and found no fix or confirmed duplicate specific to #50158.

information_gaps.information: Whether GPU and Network icons are still missing on the first released build containing merged PR #50231, and which Command Palette presentation is affected.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes an already-shipped shared grid rendering correction from a remaining glyph-specific or list-template defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Update to the current PowerToys release, open Performance Monitor in list, grid, and gallery views, and provide one screenshot naming the affected presentation.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after reproducing the current-build failure, if it persists.
information_gaps.why_needed: It may reveal font/resource initialization or extension-load evidence that the older archive did not expose.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce the missing GPU and Network icons, then add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward and attach the generated ZIP.

design.root_cause: The public report now narrows the missing visuals to the GPU and Network Performance Monitor glyphs. The provider maps those metrics to U+E950 and U+EC05, but current evidence cannot establish whether those glyphs fail to resolve in the packaged icon font or whether the shared CmdPal grid FontIcon layout clips them.
evidence: The reporter explicitly identified GPU and Network in the current live discussion.
Icons.cs defines GpuIcon as U+E950 and NetworkIcon as U+EC05.
PerformanceMonitorCommandsProvider routes GPU, Network, and NetworkSpeed through those definitions.
PR #50231 documents a distinct CmdPal grid/gallery FontIcon clipping and recycled-container loss fix.
There is no current-build reproduction or linked fix proving which rendering boundary causes this report.

implementation_steps.change: Create a deterministic fixture that supplies GPU and Network items from the Performance Monitor provider, opens each supported presentation, and asserts a visible icon element with the expected glyph source. Add a recycled-container pass after changing pages or scrolling.

If the reporter still reproduces, inspect a fresh /bugreport archive captured immediately after the visible failure.
risks: Replacing glyphs without proving packaged-font availability could alter established icon meaning.
A broad layout change could regress unrelated extension icons or virtualized grid performance.
The report may already be fixed by PR #50231, making a new source change redundant.
alternatives: Treat the report as already fixed by PR #50231. Rejected because the reporter has not tested a release containing that merged change.
Request only another generic diagnostic archive. Rejected because the live discussion now provides concrete GPU and Network targets that support focused code investigation.
Change all Performance Monitor icons to image assets. Rejected because it expands packaging and theming scope without evidence that the Fluent glyph path is fundamentally unsuitable.

comment.body:
Thanks for confirming that the missing Performance Monitor icons are GPU and Network. Current source maps those entries to specific Fluent glyphs, and a later Command Palette change fixed a separate grid/gallery FontIcon clipping issue. To determine whether this remains a GPU/Network glyph problem or was already addressed by that shared rendering fix, please:

1. Update to the current PowerToys release and check Performance Monitor in list, grid, and gallery views. Provide one screenshot identifying any view where either icon is still missing.
2. If it still reproduces, reproduce it once more and add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately afterward with the generated ZIP attached. That will help distinguish glyph loading from container rendering.
